description.text: Founded by the Swift meat packing interests and the Darling family in 1882, Darling Ingredients Inc. (“Darling”, and together with its subsidiaries, the “Company” or “we,” “us” or “our”) was incorporated in Delaware in 1962 under the name “Darling-Delaware Company, Inc.” Darling changed its name from “Darling-Delaware Company, Inc.” to “Darling International Inc.” on December 28, 1993, and from “Darling International Inc.” to “Darling Ingredients Inc.” on May 6, 2014. The address of Darling's principal executive office is 5601 N MacArthur Boulevard, Irving, Texas, 75038, and its telephone number at this address is (972) 717-0300.

about.description_short: A pioneer in circularity, Darling Ingredients Inc. (NYSE: DAR) takes material from the animal agriculture and food industries, and transforms them into valuable ingredients that nourish people, feed animals and crops, and fuel the world with renewable energy. The company operates over 260 facilities in more than 15 countries and processes about 15% of the world's animal agricultural by-products, produces about 30% of the world's collagen (both gelatin and hydrolyzed collagen), and is one of the largest producers of renewable energy.

analysis_md:
# DAR — Darling Ingredients Inc.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-20 (engine 5.5.0). Price $60.52 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $9.693B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The world's largest renderer: it collects animal by-products and used cooking oil at 260+ facilities in 15+ countries and converts them into Feed, Food (collagen/gelatin via Rousselot and Gelnex) and Fuel ingredients. It also holds 50% of Diamond Green Diesel (DGD), the 50/50 renewable-diesel JV with Valero (~1.2B gallons/year capacity), equity-method accounted — Darling's cash from DGD arrives as distributions inside operating cash flow, not as consolidated revenue. Latest FY (ended 2026-01-03) revenue was $6,135,877,000.

## Owner's earnings
Two definitions, from financials_history.csv:
- **Conservative (OCF − capex − SBC):** latest FY OCF $1,059,719,000 − capex $380,489,000 (PP&E $380,477,000 + intangible purchases $12,000, rollup tag) − SBC $21,800,000 = **$657,430,000 = $4.10/share**. OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years.
- **Maintenance (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC):** latest FY $80,730,000 — far below the conservative figure, and the distorted one of the pair: latest-FY net income ($62,804,000) carries non-cash equity-method losses from DGD's weak 2025 while the OCF series captures the cash DGD actually distributed. The OCF-based conservative series is used throughout.
- **Base used = normalized: median of the last 3 FY OE/share = $3.01** (FY2023 $1.90, FY2024 $3.01, latest FY $4.10; base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The three years are individually noisy — FY2023 was depressed by a capex spike in Darling's own PP&E line ($557,004,000 vs $332,481,000–$380,489,000 in the two later years; the project-level driver is not itemized in the committed record, and it is not DGD construction — DGD's capex sits outside Darling's capex line under the equity method, as noted below), FY2024's OCF was flattered by a $411,068,000 working-capital release, and the latest FY's OCF reflects fat/protein price strength plus the start of DGD's recovery. The median is the least-distorted single base available; see BASE_DIVERGENCE and the method range below.
- Net debt (latest): $3,848,789,000 (debt $3,937,460,000 − cash $88,671,000), plus lease liabilities $224,107,000. Management reported reducing net debt by $223.0M in Q2 2026 alone and receiving $280.0M of cash distributions from DGD in that quarter (Q2 2026 earnings release).

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: scale and route-density in rendering are real barriers, but the output is commodity-priced and a large earnings leg (DGD) is policy-priced. Evidence first: the `roic_proxy` series in fundamentals.json runs 15.1% → 12.2% → 9.8% → 4.4% → 2.5% over the last five fiscal years — falling through the cycle, not holding above the cost of capital — while gross margin stayed in a narrow 22.4–26.2% band (24.0% latest FY; 26.3% on fundamentals' TTM through 2026-07-04). Stable margin share on commodity volume with declining returns on a growing, acquisition-built asset base is a scale moat, not a pricing-power moat.
- FOR: largest global renderer — ~15% of the world's animal by-products, 260+ facilities; collection route density and rendering-plant permitting are hard to replicate; integrated captive feedstock (animal fats, used cooking oil) makes DGD a structurally low-cost renewable diesel producer; collagen/gelatin scale (Rousselot, Gelnex) at roughly 30% of global collagen supply with growing food/health demand; flexibility to route fats between feed, food and fuel markets captures value across cycles.
- AGAINST: commodity price-taker — fat, protein and renewable diesel prices are set by markets, not by Darling; DGD earnings are policy-dependent (RIN values, LCFS, 45Z production credits, small-refinery exemptions); ROIC proxy fell 15.1% → 2.5% over the last five fiscal years; leverage — net debt $3,848,789,000 is 8.0x normalized OE; acquisition-built growth (Valley Proteins, Gelnex, FASA) carries goodwill/integration risk.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-20)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine blend is 10.20%, but its components are 5-yr revenue CAGR 11.42% (acquisition-inflated — Valley Proteins closed into the 2022 revenue jump), 3-yr revenue CAGR −2.06%, latest revenue YoY +7.36%, and a 2-yr OE/share CAGR of 46.52% that is a trough artifact (FY2023's $1.90/share was capex-spike-depressed). Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets −14/−7/−3/+2/+9pp vs the blend to −3.8 / 3.2 / **7.2** / 12.2 / 19.2%: the 7.2% base start sits between the negative 3-yr revenue trend and the current prints (fundamentals TTM revenue through 2026-07-04 $6,548,664,000; Q2 2026 net sales $1.7B vs $1.5B a year earlier, per the Q2 2026 release), crediting DGD normalization from its trough and collagen growth, but not extrapolating Q2 2026's DGD print ($389.2M of EBITDA to Darling at $2.23/gallon, including a ~$51M IEEPA tariff recovery at the entity level — a policy/one-off-inflated quarter). Probabilities shifted bearish vs default (12/28/30/20/10) for the 8.0x leverage and the policy binary in DGD; OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 12% | −3.8% | 0.75 | RIN/45Z support rolls back, DGD margins return to trough, fat prices soften against 8.0x leverage | $14.23 | 5.24% |
| Bear | 28% | 3.2% | 0.90 | DGD mid-cycle at best, core ingredients grow at volume pace | $22.87 | 7.25% |
| Base | 30% | 7.2% | 1.00 | DGD normalizes below the Q2 2026 spike; collagen and fat pricing carry modest OE growth | $30.00 | 8.87% |
| Bull | 20% | 12.2% | 1.10 | 2026–27 RVO support holds, DGD stays strong, deleveraging compounds per-share OE | $40.54 | 11.15% |
| Super bull | 10% | 19.2% | 1.25 | Sustained $2+/gallon DGD economics plus SAF ramp and rapid deleveraging | $61.24 | 15.13% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $31.34 (−48.2% vs the $60.52 price), IV@12% $41.96, IV@10% $53.83, weighted IRR 9.21%, base-case IRR 8.87%.**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 4.97%, terminal value 19.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.30x, net debt 7.98x normalized OE, 9.5 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $31.34 · 20% at $21.86 · 25% at $16.67.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 2026-01-03, ~10 months ago): ttm.py was run and **exits 3 on its capex leg: "capex: no post-FY YTD fact"**. The 10-Qs themselves exist — Q1 and Q2 of the current fiscal year (periods ended 2026-04-04 and 2026-07-04, filed 2026-05-08 and 2026-08-07, per profile.json) — and fundamentals.json assembles a TTM through 2026-07-04 from them, but its TTM capex leg is likewise null: neither assembly extracts a usable post-FY YTD capex figure under the candidate tags (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets, PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment), and ttm.py is the only tool that may build an owner's-earnings TTM base. (The exit-3 parenthetical "no 10-Q since the 2026-01-03 fiscal year end" is the tool's shorthand for the missing capex fact, not a missing filing.) So no ttm.json exists and no --ttm pin was used; the normalized median base stands. Partial cross-check from fundamentals.json (a different assembly): TTM through 2026-07-04 shows revenue $6,548,664,000, OCF $1,351,407,000 and net income $597,928,000 — the current run-rate is stronger than the latest FY, which is captured in the method range below rather than in the base, because the missing capex leg is exactly what an owner's-earnings TTM cannot skip.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $4.10 vs 3-yr median $3.01): neither is clean, and they bracket the truth — FY2023 ($1.90, in the median window) was capex-spike-distorted downward, the latest FY is flattered by strong fat/protein pricing and early DGD recovery, and the median year itself (FY2024, $3.01) had a $411,068,000 working-capital release inside its OCF. The median is used as the normalized base; the latest-FY sensitivity is quantified under Thoughts.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024, 2026): 2024 — net income $278,880,000 vs OCF $839,289,000 (a +$560,409,000 gap): the lines statements.json itemizes bridge to $483,623,000 (D&A +$503,825,000, SBC +$20,918,000, deferred taxes −$122,284,000, receivables build −$179,835,000, payables −$17,881,000). The remaining +$355,666,000 sits in statement lines the committed extracts do not itemize: the working-capital release beyond the two itemized lines is bounded by the engine's balance-sheet delta_nwc (−$411,068,000 for 2024 — a release on its broader all-current-items definition, against −$197,716,000 for the two itemized lines), and the balance is the Diamond Green Diesel equity-method pair (Darling's share of DGD earnings is deducted in the reconciliation; the cash distributions it received are added) and other non-cash lines, which cannot be separated further from the committed record. Recurrence: D&A and the DGD pair recur every year by construction; the working-capital release does not — it reversed in the latest FY (delta_nwc +$110,089,000, an absorption). No tax-deposit or impairment one-off sits in the gap; it is a non-cash/equity-method and working-capital story, and the OE base uses OCF as filed either way. 2026 — net income $62,804,000 vs OCF $1,059,719,000 (a +$996,915,000 gap): the itemized lines bridge to $567,380,000 (D&A +$508,504,000, SBC +$21,795,000, deferred taxes −$103,175,000, receivables release +$50,085,000, payables build +$27,367,000). The remaining +$492,339,000 is the in-period Diamond Green Diesel equity-method pair and other lines the extracts do not itemize: net income carries Darling's share of DGD's weak-2025 losses (non-cash, added back in the reconciliation) while OCF records the cash distributions DGD actually paid during the fiscal year; the definitional difference between the engine's balance-sheet delta_nwc (+$110,089,000, an absorption) and the two itemized working-capital lines (+$77,452,000 released) also nets inside the residual. The pair recurs every year — the earnings leg flips sign with DGD's cycle (a deduction in 2024, an add-back of losses in the latest FY) while the distributions leg adds cash in both — and that pair, not any one-off, is the standing engine of this filer's NI↔OCF gap. (The $280.0M of DGD distributions cited elsewhere in this analysis is a Q2 2026 figure, after this fiscal year end, and plays no part in this bridge.) The OCF-based conservative OE is unaffected by the divergence in both years.
- **SBC_TAG_RECONCILED**: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense exceeds ShareBasedCompensation by 0.0–0.1% in FY2017, FY2018, FY2023 and FY2026 (e.g. FY2026 $21,800,000 used vs $21,795,000) — tag rounding under 1%, one line as instructed; the Allocated figure was used.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.30x): real — the DGD policy/margin swing is genuinely binary (DGD EBITDA to Darling was $42.6M in Q2 2025 vs $389.2M in Q2 2026, per Zacks' summary of the releases). Confidence is **low**, and the verdict is sized to the bear end.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt $3,848,789,000 = 7.98x normalized OE): real leverage, stated from the filing balance sheet (debt $3,937,460,000 vs cash $88,671,000, plus $224,107,000 of lease liabilities outside the net-debt figure). It is the reason probabilities were shifted bearish and the super-bear case carries a 0.75 OE multiplier; management reported $223.0M of net-debt reduction in Q2 2026 and has guided to ending 2026 at or below $3B of net debt, which would ease but not remove this flag.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear D 7.25% vs bull C 11.15%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — both ends sit below the 15% hurdle at $60.52, so the band does not change the conclusion, only its confidence.

## My thoughts / overlay
- **Method range is the honest headline:** on the normalized median base the weighted result is Tier D (9.21%, IV@15% $31.34); re-running the identical scenarios on the latest-FY base of $4.10/share (--measure sensitivity, same moat/probs/offsets) gives Tier C — weighted IRR 11.51%, IV@15% $42.74, scenario IRRs 6.27% / 8.97% / 11.09% / 14.01% / 18.97%. The full generated output of that run is committed as dcf_numbers_sensitivity_latest_fy.json (a --measure run at the same $60.52 price with identical moat/probs/offsets and --base-oe-ps pinned to the latest-FY figure); it reproduces every figure in this bullet. Both methods sit below the $60.52 price at a 15% hurdle; the disagreement is about how overvalued, not whether.
- The market is pricing the bull leg: the stock has roughly doubled from its October 2025 level (~$30) on the DGD recovery, and at $60.52 a buyer needs Q2 2026's $2.23/gallon DGD economics — struck at peak RIN/diesel spreads and including a ~$51M tariff recovery — to be the new normal rather than a policy-cycle peak. DGD has printed $0.34/gallon within the last year; that range is the whole investment question.
- The core ingredients business is the ballast: TTM gross margin 26.3% (fundamentals.json), collagen demand growing, and Q2 2026 core execution strong enough that management guided Q3 core ingredients EBITDA of $325–340M (earnings call, as reported). If DGD merely normalizes instead of collapsing, the bear cases here are too harsh — but "normalizes" at $1.00/gallon vs the $2.23 print is still a large earnings step-down from what the price embeds.
- Deleveraging is the fastest self-help lever: at the Q2 2026 pace ($223M of net-debt reduction in one quarter, $73M of buybacks), net debt/OE compresses quickly and per-share OE compounds faster than total OE — the bull cases credit this; a policy reversal at DGD would stop it, which is why leverage and DGD policy are the same risk, not two risks.
- Minority/equity note: DGD is a 50% equity-method JV, so consolidated OE captures only Darling's share via distributions — no minority-interest haircut applies to the OE series, but DGD's own capex is also outside Darling's capex line; DGD distributions are net of JV-level reinvestment, which is the correct owner's-earnings treatment.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 9.21% on the normalized base; method range D to C across the two defensible bases)
- Confidence: **low** (WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD, HIGH_NET_DEBT, and a TTM base that ttm.py could not build)
- One-liner: Real but narrow moat (5/10) in a commodity/policy-levered business — does not clear 15% at $60.52: weighted IRR 9.21% on the normalized base, IV@15% $31.34; the 15% hurdle-clearing price is ~$31 on the normalized base and ~$43 on the latest-FY base (IV@15% $42.74; that method tops out at Tier C, 11.51% at today's price).
